headline: Reviewed $9.2 million FY2026 budget surplus and proposed $6 million bond for 73 city vehicles.
summary: The unaudited year-end report showed a $9.2 million budget surplus. The committee also reviewed several grants, a library donation, and a $6 million bond authorization for the first year of the Vehicle Replacement Plan. The minutes do not record any votes or final outcomes.

Minutes: 
On October 5, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to review 
the FY2026 June Revenue and Expenditure Report and other financial items. The unaudited 
year-end report showed a $9.2 million budget surplus, including approximately $3.8 million in 
favorable revenue and $5.4 million in expenditure savings. The City plans to submit its year-end 
information to the Department of Revenue in November for certification of FY2026 free cash.
Revenue results included favorable variances of approximately $2.9 million in motor vehicle 
excise tax, $3.3 million in charges for services, and $2.3 million in investment earnings. Charges 
for services included $544,000 from the sale of City-owned property at 135-155 Lyman Street, 
$6.4 million in municipal Medicaid payments, and $1.5 million in McKinney-Vento 
transportation reimbursements. On the expenditure side, approximately $2.7 million in savings 
resulted from salaries, including $670,000 in the Police Department and $197,000 in the Fire 
Department. 
 
The committee also reviewed a $75,000 Massachusetts Gaming Commission grant for 
community-engaged research on gambling-related harms; a $75,000 Greening the Gateway 
Cities Implementation Grant for tree watering and maintenance; Crisis Intervention Team 
training reimbursement for Police and dispatch personnel; Jail Arrest Diversion Program funding 
for crisis clinicians responding to 911 calls; a $48 prior-year Labor Relations bill requiring 
payment from current-year funds; and a $100 donation to the Library from Barbara J. Gardner. 
 
The committee reviewed a proposed $6 million bond authorization for the first year of the City’s 
five-year Vehicle Replacement Plan. The funding would support 73 vehicles across the Police 
Department, Fire Department, General Fund departments, and Enterprise Fund. The committee 
noted that the plan had previously received detailed review at the Joint Maintenance & 
Development and Finance Committee meeting.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 5:13 p.m.
